tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: The workspace this key belongs to: its id, name and plan, and this period's usage.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Plan, runs used this billing period, included runs, extra-run packs and runs left.

tools.name: get_network
tools.description: How our browsers reach your sites: the static addresses to allow-list, the country they browse from, and the countries available.

tools.name: set_browse_from
tools.description: Choose the country our browsers visit your sites from (web tests), or automatic: the site's own country.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The projects in this workspace (a project groups the tests of one site or app).

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project, for example one per site or app.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Rename a project or change its description.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: Archive a project: its tests stop running; past runs stay in the run history.

tools.name: list_tests
tools.description: The tests of a project, each with its latest run.

tools.name: get_test
tools.description: One test: its start address, requirement, plan, options and latest run.

tools.name: create_test
tools.description: Create a test of a website (url) or of an app (platform android or ios, and appId; device phone or tablet and osVersion, default a phone on the latest OS). Pass `plan` (from plan_test, after the requester confirmed it): it is stored as the approved checklist and the tester follows it as written. Or

tools.name: update_test
tools.description: Change a test: its title, start address, requirement, plan or options. Only the fields you pass change; within `options`, only the options you pass change and the others keep their values.

tools.name: delete_test
tools.description: Archive a test: it stops running; past runs stay in the run history.

tools.name: plan_test
tools.description: Have the assistant draft a test from a plain-language description, or revise a plan, without saving anything. Returns the proposed steps, checks, values to record, assumptions and any questions only the requester can answer. Show the plan to the requester; to change it, call again with `plan` and `c

tools.name: list_test_files
tools.description: Files a test can upload during its steps (for example an import file).

tools.name: add_test_file
tools.description: Add a file the tester can upload during the test: up to 25 MB, up to 10 files per test. REST: send the raw bytes as the body with the file name in the X-File-Name header (or ?name=), or JSON {name, contentBase64}. MCP: name and contentBase64. A file with the same name replaces the old one.

tools.name: delete_test_file
tools.description: Remove one of a test's files.

tools.name: list_credentials
tools.description: The sign-in accounts stored for a project: names, usernames and sites. Passwords are never returned.

tools.name: add_credential
tools.description: Store a sign-in account the tester can use. The password is encrypted, never returned, and never sent to the tester's AI: the tester types it. Tests refer to the account by name ("Sign in as the account \"customer\""). Through MCP the password passes through your AI agent: prefer adding passwords in

tools.name: delete_credential
tools.description: Delete a sign-in account. Tests that sign in with it stop running until it is added again or they are edited.

tools.name: list_endpoints
tools.description: Calls into your own systems the tester may make during a run (for example "create a voucher"). Headers are never returned.

tools.name: add_endpoint
tools.description: Add a call the tester may make into your system. It sees only the name, the description and what the call returned. Using endpoints in a run needs a paid plan. bodyTemplate may contain {{param}} placeholders the tester fills in. Headers (for example Authorization) are encrypted and never returned.

tools.name: delete_endpoint
tools.description: Delete an endpoint.

tools.name: run_test
tools.description: Start a run of one test. Runs take minutes: poll get_run until final is true. watchUrl opens the run live without signing in. App tests run the newest build of their app unless buildId names another (see list_builds). watchUrl is a view-only link anyone can open (no sign-in) to watch the run live an

tools.name: run_project
tools.description: Start a run of every test in a project (a suite). Each started run has a watchUrl to watch it live without signing in. buildIds: builds to use; each app test runs the one of its own app. Tests that could not start are listed in skipped with the reason. REST: send an Idempotency-Key header to make a

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Recent runs, newest first, optionally for one test or project or with one status; or the runs with the given ids.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: A run: its status, and once final the verdict, the headline, each check's result with the reason, the values read, and links to the video, screenshots and the result page.

tools.name: wait_run
tools.description: Wait up to seconds (default 25, at most 55) for a run to finish, then return it: one call instead of polling get_run every few seconds. Call it again while final is false. The answer comes back the moment the run is final (verdict, checks and evidence in), or when the time is up with final false — t

tools.name: stop_run
tools.description: Stop a queued or running run. A run you stop is not counted.

tools.name: create_watch_link
tools.description: A view-only link to watch a run live and read its result, with no sign-in, valid while it runs and for some hours after. Runs started here get one automatically; this makes another, or one for a run started from the web app. The link shows the live screen, the steps and checks so far, then the read-

tools.name: revoke_watch_link
tools.description: Turn off every watch link of a run straight away.

tools.name: list_share_links
tools.description: The share links made for a run, with when they expire and how often they were opened.

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: A read-only link to a run's result, replay and video that anyone can open without signing in, until it expires.

tools.name: delete_share_link
tools.description: Turn off a share link straight away.

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: When tests run by themselves: every schedule in the workspace, or those of one test or project.

tools.name: create_schedule
tools.description: Run a test by itself: on chosen weekdays, or monthly on a day, at a time in a time zone. Each scheduled run counts like any other run.

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Pause or resume a schedule.

tools.name: delete_schedule
tools.description: Delete a schedule.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: The phones and tablets app tests can run on, and their OS versions (latest first). Pass device and osVersion to create_test, update_test, run_test or run_project. tools.name: list_builds
tools.description: The app builds uploaded to a project (Android .apk, iOS Simulator .app zipped), newest first, with the largest size and part size for uploads.

tools.name: get_build
tools.description: One build: its app id, version, status and any warnings.

tools.name: find_build
tools.description: Is this build already uploaded? Looks up the project's newest ready build by the file's sha256, else by a native fingerprint; build is null when neither matches. tools.description: Start a build upload and get signed links that upload the file without an API key: run the returned command in a shell, or PUT each part and POST complete to the links. The build is then checked and ready to run. For AI agents: tool arguments cannot carry a build, so hand the bytes to a shell comman

tools.name: import_build
tools.description: Fetch a build from an https link (an EAS, Bitrise, S3 or GitHub artifact link, up to the build size limit) into the project; it is checked and ready to run. tools.description: Finish the upload with every part's etag. The build is checked (app id, version, whether our devices can run it) and returned. tools.name: delete_build
tools.description: Delete a build. Runs that used it keep their results; a build a test pins cannot be deleted.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: plan_test, create_build_upload · Private data: create_test, plan_test, list_test_files, add_test_file, delete_test_file, list_credentials, add_credential, delete_credential, find_build, create_build_upload, import_build, complete_build_upload · Public sink: list_test_files, add_test_file, run_test, run_project, list_share_links, create_share_link, delete_share_link, create_build_upload, import_build, complete_build_upload · Destructive: get_usage, delete_project, list_tests, get_test, create_test, delete_test, delete_test_file, delete_credential, list_endpoints, add_endpoint, delete_endpoint, run_test, run_project, get_run, wait_run, stop_run, create_watch_link, revoke_watch_link, list_share_links, create_share_link, delete_share_link, list_schedules, create_schedule, delete_schedule, list_devices, find_build, create_build_upload, import_build, complete_build_upload, delete_build.
